result.title: RLVR Sharpens the Pencil, Not the Mind
result.summary: Models like DeepSeek-R1 made Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) famous: reward a model for correct answers and it gets dramatically better at reasoning without being taught how. The leading explanation is sharpening---that the base model already knows how to solve these problems and RLVR just makes it more likely to reach for its best solution paths. This has only ever been checked by comparing before and after training, never by watching what changes inside across it. We tracked OLMo-2-1B across all 13 training checkpoints on GSM8K. First-try accuracy climbs from 58.0% to 61.3%, but ask the model 256 times and solution coverage actually rises from 94.5% to 96.9%, proving the knowledge was already there. We then planted reasoning mistakes into problems and trained simple probes to detect them. Those probes held between AUROC 0.798 and 0.840 across all 13 checkpoints and 3 error types, a spread smaller than the confidence interval; the model never builds a sharper internal picture of what a reasoning mistake looks like. The one place we find real internal change is at the final answer token, where a probe distinguishing early from late checkpoints hits an AUROC of 0.93, while the same probe on the actual reasoning steps lands near chance. RLVR makes the model lead with its best thinking. It does not change what that thinking is.

AI.brief_summary: 论文对 OLMo-2-1B 在 GSM8K 上全部 13 个 RLVR 检查点做诊断，结合多次采样覆盖率与注入错误后的探针检测，检验「RLVR 只是锐化已有解法」这一解释，发现内部错误表征几乎不变、真实变化集中在最终答案 token。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本设定不直接属于视觉 latent 推理，但其训练前后内部表征探针与错误类型检测思路可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据是否真正进入 latent 状态、以及 RL 训练是否只改变输出选择而非推理状态本身。
